hints.title: Preserve Book Sequence
hints.text: Because books must remain in their original sequence, placing the i-th book on the current shelf involves considering which previous books share that shelf.

hints.title: Lookback Shelf Formation
hints.text: Let subproblem state i be the minimum total height for the first i books. Iterate backwards from book i to form the final shelf as long as width accommodates.

hints.title: Height Transition
hints.text: For each valid lookback book j, state i is the minimum over state j minus 1 plus the maximum book height encountered in that shelf slice.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minHeightShelves(self, books: list[list[int]], shelfWidth: int) -> int:
        n = len(books)
        dp = [float('inf')] * (n + 1)
        dp[0] = 0
        
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            width = 0
            height = 0
            for j in range(i, 0, -1):
                width += books[j - 1][0]
                if width > shelfWidth:
                    break
                height = max(height, books[j - 1][1])
                dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[j - 1] + height)
        return dp[n]
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy shelf filling is suboptimal because placing a book on a new shelf early may force a subsequent taller book into an even worse shelf.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A 1D table of size N + 1 evaluates all valid last-shelf partitionings in O(N^2) total operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that preserving order simplifies the problem to finding partition boundaries.
complexity.notes: Total height of a shelf is determined by its tallest book.
